subject: trekkies
one_liner: A PC game store for Star Trek fans who need to own every expansion before explaining why none of it counts.
brand_voice_notes: Write as a straight-faced PC game store. Build jokes from completionist buying, fan authenticity and Steam reviews. Make every consequence understandable without Star Trek lore. The fan spends money to document inaccuracies, makes their own game unusable with a mod, and keeps playing a game they publicly condemn. Edition prices are one-time fictional purchases. Use original ships and insignia.
demo_screen_concept: A Captain’s Chair game-store detail screen. Standard ($19), Command ($34) and Fleet ($59) include one, two and five ships with 100, 200 and 500 achievements. Selecting an edition updates price and ships. Add to cart shows the matching one-time total. Fleet displays a Complete Collection badge even though the customer disputes one ship. Tabs show achievements, a community mod that replaces menu labels with unreadable alien lettering, and a 286-hour Not recommended review about bridge windows. An English reference can cover the planet to make the mod usable. Keep edition deep links, keyboard tabs, cart removal and reset working at desktop and mobile widths.

hero.h1: Buy the entire galaxy. Dispute one window.
hero.sub: Shoreleave is a PC game store for Star Trek fans. Collect starship expansions, install alien-language menus and leave a 286-hour negative review because the bridge windows are wrong.

features.title: Complete your collection.
features.blurb: Buy all four ship expansions so your library finally says Complete Collection. You now own every version of the bridge you insist the developers got wrong. Your review includes screenshots from all five.

features.title: Install community mods.
features.blurb: Replace the menus with your favourite alien alphabet. Finally, a bridge that feels authentic. You cannot read it, so you tape an English translation over the planet you came to explore.

features.title: Warn the other players.
features.blurb: Post Not recommended after 286 hours because the bridge has the wrong windows. Six fans buy it to check. Your warning has started a seven-person inspection of a fictional window.

testimonials.title: Completionist; weekend starship captain

testimonials.quote: I installed the alien-language mod and got stuck in Settings. My daughter got me out by clicking things at random. She is now our translator.

testimonials.title: Convention costume maker; office manager

testimonials.quote: I posted a screenshot proving the bridge windows were wrong. Someone said my graphics settings were wrong. I bought a new monitor to settle it.
testimonials.name: Martin Ellis
testimonials.title: Local Star Trek club organiser; dissatisfied player

observations.behavior: Completionist fans buy content they reject as authentic.
observations.mechanic: Game bundles, DLC ownership and Complete Collection badge.
observations.consequence: Own all five versions of the supposedly incorrect bridge and pay to document the errors.

observations.behavior: Fans prioritize authenticity over practical use.
observations.consequence: Need a translation sheet that obscures the world they wanted to explore.

observations.behavior: A committed fan publicly warns others away while continuing to play.
observations.mechanic: Negative reviews with visible playtime and club replies.
observations.consequence: The warning sells six copies and turns the reviewer into host of a window inspection.

source_product_patterns: A PC game storefront with illustrated game listings and individual purchase prices
A game-detail page combining screenshots, description, review summary and purchase options
Base games and expansion bundles sold as progressively larger editions
An owned-game library with playtime and achievement progress
Community workshop listings for player-made modifications
Public recommended or not-recommended reviews accompanied by hours played
An edition selector and cart summary that preserve the selected purchase
editorial_plan.composition_plan: Primary action: choose a game edition. Open with a recognizable store detail preview, screenshot, collection progress and purchase panel. Features explain complete ownership despite disputed authenticity, unreadable authentic menus and a negative review that recruits window inspectors. Campaign art shows three editions and one obsessive inspection; translation artwork explains the menu problem. Both pages share the retro space manual identity.

references.reference: The bridge consoles in Star Trek: The Next Generation
references.cues: Dark control surfaces, broad rounded color bands, apricot and lavender accents, compact information groups and generous black gaps.
references.application: Use dark plum store panels with apricot primary actions and lavender selection states. Rounded bands organize screenshots, purchase information and progress. Develop original shapes and lettering without reproducing a canonical console or insignia.

references.reference: Star Trek: The Next Generation Technical Manual
references.cues: Pale technical pages, carefully captioned diagrams, condensed headings, numbered references and disciplined alignment.
references.application: Give the landing page a warm off-white manual surface, Barlow Condensed headings and Source Sans 3 body text. Number feature evidence and align captions with their images. Present the English menu reference as a practical diagram sheet.

audience_design.landing_application: Combine the manual's pale pages with inset bridge-console product panels. Use warm off-white #F3EFE6, dark plum #252133, apricot #E5A16C and muted lavender #B5A0D8. Barlow Condensed supplies compact display headings; Source Sans 3 handles explanations, prices and controls. Original game screenshots provide the main imagery, with the domestic reference-sheet photograph supporting the second feature. Use a broad opening store preview, clear horizontal section divisions and an aligned edition table. Keep body text in ordinary sentence case and reserve numbering for useful references.
audience_design.demo_application: Increase information density inside the same plum, apricot and lavender system. Preserve the game store's screenshot gallery, purchase sidebar, edition selector, achievement progress, community-mod listing and playtime-bearing reviews. Use readable rectangular controls inside the larger rounded panel groups. The audience references affect typography, color and framing while the store workflow remains easy to recognize. Keep the English reference control legible when the fictional menu translation is active.

design_direction.style: Retro-futurist technical manual: pale captioned pages with dark plum bridge-console insets and broad interrupted rounded bands.

palette.name: Manual Paper, Bridge Plum, Apricot and Lavender

fonts.pairing: Bundled Sports/Fitness Barlow Condensed display combined with Corporate Trust Source Sans 3 body; preserves both host-approved fonts.

design_direction.archetype: PC game storefront landing with a broad screenshot-and-purchase preview, manual-style feature evidence, composed graphic spreads, player accounts and joined edition comparison.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 150ms color feedback and deliberate tab or selection state changes; no ambient animation. Reduced-motion removes transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: A clear game-store proposition followed by a broad starship screenshot and adjacent edition purchase panel. Show one of five ships owned, collection badge, one-time prices and readable reviews. On mobile stack screenshot before purchasing controls.
design_direction.design_review: All seven supplied digest identities compared. No matching style/palette/fonts tuple. Interrupted command bands and an empty captain chair differ from prize rosettes, train sidings, yearbook cursor, cabinets, salvage tags, album sleeves and pond contours. Retain library preview/content hierarchy and accessible UI rules; reject generic vibrant community blocks, neon purple and Exo/Roboto Mono because the approved manual/bridge references are authoritative.

generation.revision_reason: User requested stronger, distinct jokes and matching replacement campaign art.
generation.logo_revision_reason: Preserve accepted identity while removing the mismatched beige background with image_gen.

brand_kit.identity_rationale: An empty captain chair makes the customer absence visible. Its broad console arms and a leave-ticket notch bridge heroic command and office leave. A bespoke narrow Shoreleave wordmark joins technical-manual typography with console curves. Artwork uses printed technical collage, not the previous entries' documentary catalogues or mascots.

logo.concept: Selected Gemini direction A: an empty apricot command chair, lavender rounded console arms and dark plum base with bespoke correctly spelled Shoreleave lettering. Stronger at nav and icon sizes than B, whose interrupted doorway reads as a generic control badge. Wordmark spelling, kerning and silhouette visually inspected.
logo.clear_space: Transparent clear space of at least half the symbol height; no painted background.
logo.placement: Landing navigation and footer, demo chrome; faithful symbol crop as favicon on both pages.

graphic_language.medium: Gemini-designed technical-manual editorial collage, paired with original cinematic 3D game stills and domestic gaming photography.
graphic_language.motif: Interrupted rounded command bands, empty command chair, and rectangular leave slips.
graphic_language.composition: 1248px content maximum; 24px desktop internal gaps; 20px mobile gutters (16px at 320px); 80px desktop sections and 48px mobile sections. Broad product preview first; two full-composition art spreads with live summaries.
graphic_language.texture: Fine uncoated-paper grain inside graphic artwork; flat pale HTML surfaces and solid dark console panels.

tokens.radii: 4px controls; 12px screenshot panels; 40px/12px asymmetric console corners; 999px status bands
tokens.borders: 1px solid var(--line); 2px solid var(--accent) for selected states

items.prompt: Design a finished original graphic artwork for Shoreleave, a fictional PC game store for Star Trek fans. Attached image is the APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE: preserve its empty apricot captain chair, lavender console arms, custom Shoreleave letterforms and dark plum contours. Art direction: premium 1990s science-fiction technical manual meets editorial paper-cut composition. Exact palette paper #F3EFE6, plum #252133, apricot #E5A16C, lavender #B5A0D8. Subtle uncoated printed grain. Professional layout hierarchy with generous negative space and bold condensed type. Original ship designs, no official Star Trek symbols or Steam marks. This is a composed graphic design deliverable, NOT a photograph, NOT a logo presentation board, NOT a plain flowchart. No gibberish, watermarks or extra words. Use only supplied text verbatim, make lettering clean and readable on mobile. Create a 4:3 landscape DESIGNED INSTRUCTION COMPOSITION with a lavender technical drawing of a starship bridge viewscreen containing a large apricot planet. A physically folded pale English reference sheet taped across the right half of that viewscreen obscures much of the planet. Use stylized invented alien glyphs as illustration on the left console. Integrate a large custom heading and a carefully aligned reference table into the right paper sheet; this should feel like an original technical-manual insert, with exploded paper edges and tape, not a primitive diagram. Exact copy, nothing else: "Authenticity installed."; "English required."; "Reference sheet"; "Navigate"; "Crew"; "Settings"; "Quit"; "Keep this over the planet."; small exact Shoreleave wordmark in bottom margin. Strong hierarchy, short large labels, clear comic cause and consequence.

items.prompt: Create one cinematic high-quality 3D PC GAME ENVIRONMENT STILL, original science-fiction starship bridge for Captain's Chair, fictional game sold by Shoreleave. Attached image is APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE for empty chair design and palette, not an image to paste. Adult 1990s television science-fiction fan aesthetic: dark plum #252133 hull and console surfaces, lavender #B5A0D8 padded arms, apricot #E5A16C chair upholstery, warm off-white trim. Wide symmetrical perspective from rear of bridge, one unmistakable EMPTY captain chair in middle foreground, sweeping ergonomic consoles, extraordinary huge warm apricot planet and moon through wide front windows, lavender atmospheric light, carefully modeled mechanical materials, gorgeous playable-game environment rather than real photography. Left foreground has a simple dark personnel terminal angled toward viewer, with BLANK dark display to allow live HTML controls later. No people, no lettering, NO TEXT, no logos, no insignia, no numbers, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens, no game HUD. No recognizable franchise-specific ship or canonical bridge, invent architecture and furniture. Keep planet visible above chair; bright detailed scene in 16:9.
items.placement: Opening storefront preview and demo screenshot gallery
items.verdict: Accepted. Empty chair matches identity; original bridge, bright planet, blank foreground terminal, no labels or insignia. Main product context clear.

items.prompt: Create an editorial documentary photograph of a real domestic PC gaming desk in a modest British spare room at evening. Attached first image is APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE for the apricot/lavender/plum design language, NOT a logo to paste. A computer monitor shows only an original 3D science-fiction bridge environment with an EMPTY APRICOT captain chair and a large orange planet, no interface, no typography. A large plain white reference page, with NO WRITING OR PRINT whatsoever, is taped across the RIGHT THIRD of the screen with two pieces of masking tape, physically hiding part of the planet. Nearby keyboard, ceramic tea mug, practical home desk and an unbranded laminating pouch. Tactile, believable slightly mundane office-photo composition, monitor dominates. No people, no text, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI controls, no icons, no words on any surface. Landscape 4:3. The gag is clearly a beautiful view of space partly blocked by a piece of domestic office paper. Natural photography, not diagram, not illustration.
items.placement: Landing player accounts beside English reference sheet
items.verdict: Accepted. Believable home desk; blank paper visibly obstructs planet. English reference labels supplied as live HTML on paper. No essential text baked into photo.

items.prompt: Use case: ads-marketing. Edit target: attached Shoreleave campaign poster. Completely replace the obsolete crew leave paperwork joke and ALL its text with a new graphic about a Star Trek fan buying game expansions only to complain about canon. Keep the professional retro space technical-manual aesthetic, warm off-white paper, lavender, apricot and dark plum, condensed bold typography. Landscape 4:3. Compose three handsome near-identical original starship models on display plinths, all identical except slightly different window arrangements. An enormous magnifying glass inspects one tiny window. No office paperwork. Exact text only: headline "Three editions. One wrong window."; ship labels "Standard", "Command", "Fleet"; lower line "Buy the expansion. Continue the argument."; small brand "Shoreleave". Legible text and beautiful editorial hierarchy, ships and type balanced. Original spaceship forms, no existing franchise logos. This replaces every mention of leave requests, 99/100 and Friday off.
items.verdict: Accepted after visual inspection for copy, meaning and brand continuity.

discarded.verdict: Rejected. Correct lettering, but abstract doorway looks like a generic badge and carries less of the premise than the chair.
